data.title: List
data.tagline: Show similar items one after another
data.description: A list repeats the same structure for messages, articles, contacts, or other items that people scan from top to bottom. It is more flexible than a table and more compact than a grid of cards, so it works when column-by-column comparison is not important.

use: A compact stream of similar content
avoid: Use it when several fields must line up for comparison
Give every row a different structure
Load an endless list without progress or a way back

lessonPractice.title: A notification center shows dozens of messages by time. Each has a title, summary, timestamp, and View action, with no need for column comparison. How should it be organized?

options.label: Use a vertical list with a consistent message structure ordered by time
options.feedback: The records share a structure and are read in sequence, so a list supports scanning and opening individual details.

options.label: Use four table columns for title, summary, time, and action
options.feedback: Tables suit comparison across fixed fields. Variable summaries become compressed and force horizontal reading.

options.label: Use a multi-column card grid and add a cover image and large icon to every message
options.feedback: Images are not the main content here. A grid interrupts chronological reading and adds irrelevant visual information.

data.agentPrompt: Change the notification center to a time-ordered vertical list. Each item should consistently show a title, a summary capped at two lines, a timestamp, and a View action. Test alignment, wrapping, and click targets with varied summary lengths.
